# Audit Requirements Checklist: Observed test-first

**Purpose**: Unit tests for the requirements of the audit's verdict rules, the ledger hook and Stop
contracts, the installer's refusals, and constitution 1.1.0's principles IV and VI as they apply to
this feature — before implementation
**Created**: 2026-10-07
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Requirement Completeness

- [x] CHK001 Is every verdict of FR-009 defined with a condition that a replay can decide, with no verdict left to judgement? [Completeness, Spec §FR-009, data-model "Verdict"]
- [x] CHK002 Is a remedy specified for every failing verdict, `not-judged` reasons included, and is each remedy an action the agent can take without the owner? [Completeness, Spec §FR-018, data-model "Verdict"]
- [x] CHK003 Are all inputs the audit may read enumerated, so that FR-012 ("never a file the agent writes as evidence") can be checked against a closed list? [Completeness, Spec §FR-012, contracts/audit.md]
- [x] CHK004 Are the hook's failure modes (git error, malformed configuration, locked repository, disk full) each specified with the agent-facing outcome? [Completeness, Spec §FR-004, contracts/ledger-hook.md]
- [x] CHK005 Are all the installer's refusal conditions listed in one place, and does each FR-014 condition appear in contracts/install-ledger.md and vice versa? [Completeness, Spec §FR-014]
- [x] CHK006 Is what the Stop entry reports when its budget runs out specified, including who sees it (user or Claude)? [Completeness, Spec §FR-024, contracts/ledger-hook.md "Stop"]
- [x] CHK007 Are the requirements for pruning scratch worktrees left by a killed audit stated as an observable outcome (nothing registered after the next run)? [Completeness, Constitution IV, contracts/audit.md]
- [x] CHK008 Is the README's limits section (FR-022) specified as a closed list that matches every stated limit in data-model.md, research.md R13–R14 and the spec's Edge Cases? [Completeness, Spec §FR-022, Constitution VI]

## Requirement Clarity

- [x] CHK009 Is "mixed" defined unambiguously for a call that changes tests, sources and other paths at once, and for a path matching both `tests` and `sources`? [Clarity, Spec §FR-005, data-model "Change"]
- [x] CHK010 Is "the test side as it stood before the call" (green check) defined precisely enough that two implementers would build the same tree? [Clarity, Spec §FR-009, data-model "Run" variants]
- [x] CHK011 Is "inconclusive" defined so that a run with zero cases, a run with no JUnit, and a load-probe match cannot be confused? [Clarity, Spec §FR-007, data-model "Run"]
- [x] CHK012 Is "first run" defined with respect to skipped outcomes, and is "never run" distinguished from "still red" in every document that names them? [Clarity, Spec §FR-008, §FR-010]
- [x] CHK013 Is "accepted verdict" defined once and used with the same meaning in `refactored` and `Restored`? [Clarity, data-model "Judged at first run", "Restored"]
- [x] CHK014 Is the count rule for `refactored` specific about what is counted (test ids, per record, across files) and which records qualify (not mixed)? [Clarity, Spec §FR-009, research R13]
- [x] CHK015 Is "imported" defined in terms the ledger records (`head`, the commit's content), without reference to how the commit was made? [Clarity, data-model "Effective history"]
- [x] CHK016 Is the base resolution order stated as a total order with a refusal at its end, and is "without network access" testable? [Clarity, Spec §FR-027, data-model "Base"]

## Requirement Consistency

- [x] CHK017 Do FR-009, data-model's verdict table, contracts/audit.md's exit codes and FR-024's blocking set agree on which verdicts fail, which block a turn, and which are listed only? [Consistency]
- [x] CHK018 Do FR-025 ("fails without any source file") and data-model step 1 agree on the verdict and reason for a test of code outside `sources`? [Consistency, Spec §FR-025]
- [x] CHK019 Are the branch rules (visits, `checkout -b`, renames, rebases) stated identically in data-model "Effective history" and the spec's Edge Cases? [Consistency]
- [x] CHK020 Do the spec's Story 1 scenarios 1–12 map one to one onto data-model rules, with no scenario whose expected verdict the rules do not produce? [Consistency, Spec §US1]
- [x] CHK021 Do contracts/ledger-hook.md and FR-024 agree on `stop_hook_active`, detached HEAD and the default branch as reasons to skip the Stop audit? [Consistency]
- [x] CHK022 Are the hook's message conditions (FR-005: test and source paths) consistent with the verdict naming (`born-with-code` uses source paths) while replays use the test side / rest partition? [Consistency, data-model "Configuration"]
- [x] CHK023 Does constitution IV's write confinement agree with every write the contracts describe (memo, scratch worktree registration, temporary directory, installer commit)? [Consistency, Constitution IV, contracts/audit.md]

## Acceptance Criteria Quality

- [x] CHK024 Are SC-001 and SC-002 stated over recorded call sequences that the quickstart names, so they can be reproduced? [Measurability, Spec §SC-001, §SC-002]
- [x] CHK025 Is SC-003's 100 ms stated with the repository size, the statistic (median of how many) and the machine? [Measurability, Spec §SC-003]
- [x] CHK026 Are SC-004's warm and cold figures distinguished, with the cold one marked as an estimate until measured? [Measurability, Spec §SC-004]
- [x] CHK027 Is SC-006 phrased so its comparison with 1.6.0 cannot be read as a like-for-like measurement? [Measurability, Spec §SC-006, Constitution III]

## Scenario Coverage

- [x] CHK028 Are requirements defined for each common honest workflow — test then code, stub then code, rename, consolidation into a parametrized test, helper refactor, commit in its own call, rebase onto main, stash and pop, the redo sequence — with the expected verdict? [Coverage, Spec §US1, quickstart]
- [x] CHK029 Are requirements defined for each code-first route L1 observed and its variants — one shell call, code one call before the test, a test edited until it passes, a helper changed until it passes, code outside `sources` first? [Coverage, Spec §US1]
- [x] CHK030 Are exception flows specified for a replay that hangs, a runner that writes no JUnit, a file that does not load at the newest record, and a before-version that does not load? [Coverage, Exception Flow]
- [x] CHK031 Are recovery requirements specified after a killed hook, a killed audit and a deleted memo, each with the state the repository is left in? [Coverage, Recovery, Constitution IV]

## Edge Case Coverage

- [x] CHK032 Are the stated limits (a changed body of an accepted test, ids added by a change outside the test file, tests imported by commits, a restored test beside different code, Go) each written as a limit rather than left implicit? [Edge Case, Spec §FR-022]
- [x] CHK033 Is the behaviour defined for a test file whose only test is removed, under runners that report a file without tests like a load failure? [Edge Case, data-model "Run"]
- [x] CHK034 Is the behaviour defined for parallel tool calls and two sessions writing in one worktree, and is the claim that the union record is "what happened" justified? [Edge Case, research R1]

## Non-Functional Requirements

- [x] CHK035 Are privacy requirements stated for what the ledger stores (uncommitted and untracked files) and for when it can leave the machine (`git push --mirror`)? [Non-Functional, Spec §FR-022, Constitution IV]
- [x] CHK036 Is the threat model (an agent taking shortcuts, not one forging the ledger) stated once and referenced wherever a rule depends on it (`refactored`, `Restored`)? [Non-Functional, research R0, Constitution VI]
- [x] CHK037 Are deadlines and budgets specified with values and with what happens when each is exceeded (per run, Stop budget, hook timeout)? [Non-Functional, Spec §FR-011, §FR-024]

## Dependencies & Assumptions

- [x] CHK038 Is every claim about Claude Code's hook behaviour (PostToolUse for subagents, exit 2 semantics, parallel Stop hooks, block cap) traced to the hooks reference with its reading date? [Assumption, research L7, Constitution III]
- [x] CHK039 Is every claim about runner output (pytest 9.1.1, Vitest 5.0.3) traced to a dated measurement with versions, and are unmeasured runners (Jest, PHPUnit) marked as unmeasured? [Assumption, Spec Assumptions, Constitution III]
- [x] CHK040 Is the assumption that replays use the environment at audit time, not at record time, stated together with its consequence for the memo? [Assumption, data-model "Run" Memo]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify`
- Items are numbered sequentially for easy reference
